name: Script Process: the Six Patterns
oneLine: Six timing patterns - Until, After, Never, Always, Almost, Open-ended - describe how any script is lived out over time, independent of its content.
whatYouDid: You caught Until playing out inside a single sentence of Teodora's - the self-interrupting parenthetical ('not just mostly finished, I mean properly done') that keeps adding one more condition before she's allowed to relax.

fromBook.quote: Study of the life-script has revealed a fascinating fact. It is that there seem to be only six main patterns of script process.

expand.definition: Each pattern has both a life-long version (retire, then I'll travel) and a short-term, moment-to-moment version (finish the dishes, then I'll sit down) - and several have a distinctive sentence structure you can hear in real time.
expand.otherFraming: Kahler ties each process pattern to a primary driver - Be Perfect to Until, Please Others to After, Be Strong to Never, Try Hard to Always - so hearing someone's driver already predicts their process pattern.
expand.tryThisToday: Catch yourself using one of the six patterns' telltale sentence structures today - the 'but' hinge of After, or the self-interrupting parenthesis of Until - and finish the sentence differently on purpose.
